---
title: "Sibling functions do not share the same default values"
ref: FUN-11
categories: [Functions]
impact: incoherent
extrait: 'formals(list.dirs)$recursive'
reponse: 'TRUE'
attendu: "`FALSE`, as for `list.files()`"
versions: "All"
source: "Slack ThinkR (2023, 2024)"
---

::: {.piege}
```{r}
root <- tempfile()
dir.create(file.path(root, "a", "b"), recursive = TRUE)
list.files(root)
list.dirs(root, full.names = FALSE)

formals(list.files)$recursive
formals(list.dirs)$recursive
names(formals(pdf))[1]
names(formals(png))[1]
```
:::

## Why

`list.files()` does not go down into subfolders by default, `list.dirs()` does. The latter also returns the starting folder itself, as an empty string when `full.names = FALSE`.

Likewise, the output file is called `file` in `pdf()` but `filename` in `png()`. These functions were written at different times, and their arguments were never harmonised.

## The fix

Write every argument you depend on, even when you think you know its default value, and check with `args()` when in doubt.

::: {.piege}
```{r}
list.dirs(root, full.names = FALSE, recursive = FALSE)
list.files(root, recursive = TRUE, include.dirs = TRUE)
args(list.dirs)
```
:::
